summary: Cast-iron tower off Winter Island at the mouth of Salem Harbor, first lit in 1871, dark after the Coast Guard left, relit as a private aid in 1983.

staffing.note: Last keeper on the archive roster is James Yates (1919); Coast Guard left the island in 1969 (1970 per LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Grounds at Winter Island Marine Park open; tower closed to visitors.

events.note: Three small harbor lights (Fort Pickering, Hospital Point, Derby Wharf) allocated funds, per LighthouseFriends
Cast-iron tower, brick-lined, joined to the island by a wooden walkway
Lit 17 January 1871 with a fifth-order Fresnel lens
Wooden walkway destroyed by ice; rebuilt
Barn rebuilt; brick cistern provided for the dwelling
Water pipes connect the dwelling to the Salem water system
Wooden walkway destroyed by ice again; rebuilt
James Yates, last name on the archive roster
Blizzard trapped about thirty Coast Guardsmen in the keeper's house until a snowplow broke through
Coast Guard airplane hangar built on Winter Island; men lived in the keeper's house
Coast Guard left the island and an offshore buoy replaced the light (LighthouseFriends gives 1970)
Blizzard tore the tower door off; it fell into the harbor and was later recovered
Relit as a private aid to navigation after restoration by the Fort Pickering Light Association
Converted to solar power in April 1995 after the power link from shore failed
Coast Guard installed a rebuilt solar system in February 2010 after a July 2009 failure

notes_for_editor: NRHP 94000335 (in the record's registers): the nomination PDF on npgallery is the 'not yet digitized' placeholder, so the register status is unverified. Keeper start for John Harris: archive 1881, LighthouseFriends December 1881, D'Entremont December 1882; the story gives all three. Coast Guard departure: 1969 (D'Entremont, Coastal Byway) against 1970 (LighthouseFriends). Height: 28 ft above sea level (LighthouseFriends, 8.5 m used in the record) against 32 ft above mean high water (archive). The 1869 appropriation, the 1871 temporary structure, the 1878 sixth-order lens and the 1879/1904 walkway losses rest on LighthouseFriends alone; the Board reports before 1891 are not in the local corpus. The Boston Daily Globe article is cited as quoted by LighthouseFriends; the Globe itself was not read. Chronicling America searches for Fort Pickering returned no usable lighthouse pages. The keeper who was dismissed over the Plummer Home job is not named in any source read. The Commissioner's list (1915 to 1922 volume) says electric incandescent, while LighthouseFriends says incandescent oil vapor by 1920; the story gives both. Harris's stint is shown by the archive as 1881 to 1919 and the archive's place page is cited for all roster lines. Archive person slugs were taken from roster.py --json. Page checks: the 1891 Board citation's printed page 45 comes from the Board's index and the OCR order (the scan shows the 46 header after item 78) and the 1895 printed page 53 likewise (index); please confirm both against the page images. The Commissioner's list is an OCR column: Fort Pickering's entry was matched by position between Egg Rock and Nobska Point, ; the page image was checked on 2026-10-22: the row sits under the heading for other lights changed from oil-wick lights, etc. (37 lights), printed p. 39 (scan 439). The 1891 entry (item 78, 'Fort Pickering, on Winter Island') falls before the page-46 running head in the OCR, and the 1895 entry (item 84) starts before the page-54 head, so printed pages 45 and 53 hold.
